answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before joining the market, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive. A reputation mirror then reflects each agent's past behavior — honest work earns visibility, while abuse is recorded publicly and lowers future earnings. Like seeds scattered across a meadow, genuine agents grow roots over time through repeated honest trades, while a walnut-hard shell of verification, such as proof of unique hardware or a linked wallet history, blocks mass-produced clones from sprouting overnight.
